breakpoints.note: The first line of the staged witness is `1 9`, so `parse_matrix_header()` succeeds and admits the file to the matrix loader. The same header path initializes output dimensions `width = 1` and `height = 9`, which makes the later row loop parse exactly one token per row.

First project-side statement on the crashing row that materializes attacker-controlled row bytes into vulnerability-relevant heap state. After the valid matrix header has admitted this loader, `vips_sbuf_get_line_copy()` copies the current untrusted data row into heap buffer `line`.

The parser frees the row buffer before reporting the conversion error. Because `p` still aliases the current token inside `line`, the subsequent `vips_error(..., p)` call uses a dangling pointer. The staged fix removes this use-after-free by moving `g_free(line)` after `vips_error(...)`.
